item.title: Get a recipe from a retired baker by ear
item.summary: An interviewer learns why weight, time and touch all matter.
item.transcript_text:
Interviewer: Would printing your recipe let someone reproduce the flatbread at home?
Baker: The weights get them close. But we made dough beside an oven that had been hot for an hour. A home kitchen might be cooler. When I say the dough feels like a folded cloth, I mean it pulls slightly before it gives. A clock can't tell you that.
Interviewer: Would a video help?
Baker: It would show the stretch. You'd still need to try it. Include the time we used as a starting point and put the felt test beside it. If the dough tears, they should know that waiting a little longer can help.
Interviewer: So the notebook records the method, and it also assumes a room and a set of hands.

questions.prompt: Why might the notebook be insufficient?
options: It gives incorrect weights for most ingredients
It assumes conditions and tactile judgement
The baker never wrote down any timings
Methods from work kitchens cannot be adapted
questions.explanation: The shop’s warmth and the feel of the dough are not fully described.

questions.prompt: What does the folded cloth image convey?
options: Resistance before the dough stretches
The colour of fully baked bread
A cloth that must cover the oven
The thickness of the whole batch
questions.explanation: The baker describes the feel as a slight pull before it gives.

options: An exact time for every kitchen
A guarantee of the correct result
Weights missing from the notebook
A visible example of the stretch
questions.explanation: It could show the stretch although direct practice still matters.

options: It removes the need to feel the dough
It is fixed by the recipe in all conditions
It provides an initial reference
It prevents all tearing
questions.explanation: The baker advises using the time as a starting point.

questions.prompt: What does the final line recognise?
options: The baker wants people to work in the original room
Written methods can leave practical knowledge implicit
A person can learn only from film
The flatbread is impossible to reproduce
questions.explanation: A written recipe can rely on conditions and tacit skill.
